1.explanation:
• Overlay bug reproduction: We wrap a DatePicker trigger with a Popup inside a DIV that has its own scrollbar, while the page body also scrolls. By passing `container={trigger => trigger.parentNode}` we force the popup to render in the scrollable container. Open the picker, scroll the container, then click the trigger again and observe the popup drifting out of alignment.  

• NumberPicker bug reproduction: We render a NumberPicker with custom `innerBefore` and attempt `innerAfter`. The prefix element is mis-positioned around the input, and the suffix is not natively supported so either disappears or breaks the input layout. This matches the style & support issues shown in the screenshots.
1.bug_scenario:
1. Overlay Positioning Bug: When you render a DatePicker (which uses Overlay.Popup under the hood) inside a scrollable container — while the page itself also has a scrollbar — the popup initially opens in the right place. However, if you scroll the inner container a little while the popup is open and then click the DatePicker trigger again, the popup mis-positions (it no longer aligns with the trigger).  

2. NumberPicker innerBefore/innerAfter Styling Bug: When you supply a custom prefix via the `innerBefore` prop, the prefix element is misaligned (wrong margin/position), and there is no built-in support for an `innerAfter` prop, so attempting to render a suffix fails or is ignored, breaking the layout.
